title: SBA Loan Tracking: How to Check Your Status, Payments, and Documents
summary: Track SBA-serviced loans in the MySBA Loan Portal at lending.sba.gov. For lender-held 7(a) and 504 loans, check status and pay through your lender.
body_markdown:
SBA loan tracking sounds simple until you learn there's no single place to do it. Where you check status, make payments, and find documents depends on who holds your loan—SBA or your lender.


This guide maps each loan situation to the right tracker. It also covers how to keep a stalled file moving, how to spot fraud, and how lenders give borrowers clearer visibility.


‍


### Where SBA Loan Tracking Happens—and Why It Depends on Your Loan


SBA loan tracking happens in two places. SBA's MySBA Loan Portal (lending.sba.gov) covers loans SBA services directly, while your lender's systems cover lender-held 7(a) and 504 loans. Disaster applicants can apply and check status in the portal—existing borrowers with eligible loans can pay and view documents there.


[SBA's portal guidance](https://www.sba.gov/about-sba/open-government/about-sbagov-website/sba-account-login-registration-portals) says borrowers applying for SBA disaster loans can use the portal to apply and check application status. SBA also lists the existing loans the portal supports: disaster loans, guaranty-purchased PPP loans, guaranty-purchased SBA-serviced 7(a) loans, and debenture-purchased 504 loans. For other SBA loans, borrowers keep using Pay.gov or their lender.


Keep the two SBA domains straight. Sba.gov is informational—program rules, guidance, and contacts. Lending.sba.gov is operational—where eligible borrowers sign in, pay, and message SBA.


#### Quick Reference: Which Tracker Fits Your Loan


Use this SBA loan tracking table to match your loan situation to the right tracker before you log in anywhere. Checking the wrong portal wastes time when you need answers fast.


Loan situation Where to track What you can do


Applying for an SBA disaster loan MySBA Loan Portal (lending.sba.gov) Apply and check application status


Existing SBA disaster loan, including COVID-19 EIDL MySBA Loan Portal (lending.sba.gov) Make payments and view loan documents


Guaranty-purchased PPP or SBA-serviced 7(a) loan MySBA Loan Portal (lending.sba.gov) Make payments and view loan documents


Debenture-purchased 504 loan MySBA Loan Portal (lending.sba.gov) Make payments and view loan documents


Lender-held 7(a) or 504 loan, in process or in repayment Your lender's portal or loan officer Check status, share documents, and arrange payments


‍


### How to Track an SBA Loan in the MySBA Loan Portal


The MySBA Loan Portal is SBA's operational hub for loans the agency services directly. It handles disaster loan applications, payments, statements, correspondence, and secure messages with SBA staff.


If your loan fits one of the portal categories above, set up access before you need it. A working login saves time when a payment is due or SBA asks for information.


#### Sign In or Register


Type lending.sba.gov directly into your browser and bookmark it—skip search ads and emailed links. First-time users click register to create an account.


Pay.gov notes that borrowers with existing CAFS or VetCert credentials can use them to sign in. If you hit a sign-in problem with a charged-off 7(a), PPP, or purchased 504 loan, call the Fresno Servicing Center listed in the FAQ below.


#### Check Status, Messages, and Documents


Disaster loan applicants can check application status after signing in. Existing borrowers can view statements and correspondence and exchange messages with the SBA team, according to the[Pay.gov borrower payment notice](https://www.pay.gov/public/form/start/3723407) .


Check your messages after every status update—SBA may request information there. Treat the inbox as part of your SBA loan tracking, alongside statements. Respond quickly and upload exactly what's asked, since open requests can hold up your file.


#### Make and Manage Payments


The portal supports one-time or recurring payments toward your SBA loan. You can also cancel recurring payments you originally created on Pay.gov.


Pay.gov's notice said the 1201 Borrower Payment Form would stop processing loan payments starting January 1, 2024, and directed borrowers to the MySBA Loan Portal. Don't submit SBA payments through other Pay.gov forms.


Portal payments apply only to the loan types SBA lists. If a bank holds your loan, pay the way your lender directs, and confirm the method in writing before your first due date.


‍


### How to Track an SBA Loan That Your Lender Holds


7(a) and 504 applications generally move through an SBA lender rather than SBA itself. For these loans, SBA loan tracking runs through your lender's portal or loan officer—they're your status source from application through servicing.


Typical stages run in order: pre-qualification, pre-approval, underwriting, packaging and closing, funding, then servicing. Timelines depend on loan size, loan purpose, third-party reports, and how ready your documentation is.


Ask targeted questions at each stage to avoid surprises. Write down each answer so you can compare it with later updates:


- At pre-qualification, ask which documents the full application requires.
- At pre-approval, ask which conditions remain before underwriting starts.
- During underwriting, ask whether any third-party reports are still pending.
- At closing, ask for a target date and a final document checklist.
- After funding, ask how and where you'll make payments.


Lenders can shorten these stages with automation. Lendflow's guide to[AI underwriting for SBA lenders](https://lendflow.com/post/ai-underwriting-tools-for-sba-lenders-how-to-choose-one-that-speeds-decisions-without-adding-risk) explains how to speed decisions without adding risk.


#### Why SBA Files Stall—and How to Keep Yours Moving


Waiting is a common friction point with lenders. The[Federal Reserve's Small Business Credit Survey](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/reports/survey/2026/2026-report-on-employer-firms) found 21% of large-bank applicants cited a long wait for a credit decision or funding. That share was 16% at small banks and 8% at online lenders.


The survey isn't SBA-specific—it covers all credit products. It's also a self-reported convenience sample fielded in fall 2025, so treat the numbers as directional.


Most stalls trace back to three causes: incomplete documents, slow replies to information requests, and pending third-party reports. You control the first two, and your lender or its vendors control the third.


Keep your file moving—upload complete documents the first time, label every file clearly, and answer lender requests fast. Ask your loan officer which third-party reports your loan needs so you can plan around them.

### Stay Safe: Verify You're on the Official SBA Portal


The SBA is a U.S. government agency, and its loan programs are legitimate.[SBA's 2025 annual report](https://www.sba.gov/annual-report/) says the agency guaranteed 85,000 7(a) and 504 loans totaling $45 billion in FY2025.


Scammers still imitate SBA, so verify every touchpoint in your SBA loan tracking routine. Use only lending.sba.gov for portal tasks, and type the address yourself.


The[SBA Inspector General's fraud guidance](https://www.sba.gov/about-sba/oversight-and-advocacy/office-of-inspector-general/protect-yourself-from-scams-and-fraud/) says SBA only communicates from email addresses ending in @sba.gov. Suspect fraud if anyone demands upfront payment to secure loan approval.


### SBA Loan Tracking FAQs


#### How do I check the status of my SBA loan application?


For disaster loans, sign in to the MySBA Loan Portal at lending.sba.gov to check application status. For 7(a) and 504 loans, ask your lender, which manages your application.


#### How long does the SBA loan process take?


It varies by loan size, loan purpose, third-party reports, and how ready your documents are. Ask your lender for an estimate based on your file.


#### Where is the official SBA loan portal?


The official MySBA Loan Portal is lending.sba.gov. Type the address directly into your browser instead of clicking emailed links.


#### How do I make payments on my SBA loan?


If your loan type is eligible, pay in the MySBA Loan Portal with one-time or recurring payments. Otherwise, use Pay.gov or follow your lender's payment instructions.


#### Where can I find my SBA loan documents?


Eligible borrowers can view statements and correspondence in the MySBA Loan Portal. For lender-held loans, request documents through your lender's portal or loan officer.


#### Can PPP loans still be forgiven?


Yes—[SBA's COVID-era program page](https://www.sba.gov/loans/covid-era-programs/) says borrowers can apply for forgiveness up to five years from the date SBA issued the loan number. Apply through SBA's direct forgiveness portal.


#### Who do I contact for SBA loan support?


Call the Fresno Servicing Center at 1-800-347-0922 for portal-account trouble with charged-off 7(a), PPP, or purchased 504 loans. For disaster loans, call 1-800-659-2955 or emaildisastercustomerservice@sba.gov , and use in-portal messages for account questions.
